title: Protesters clash with police and burn historic town hall in Limoges
seoTitle: Limoges town hall burned during protests

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated against high living costs, systemic inequality, and excessive police force.
tea.want: Lower living costs, addressing systemic inequality, and changes to government and policing policies.
tea.changed: Oct 18: Authorities reported over 1,200 arrests nationwide following widespread clashes and the burning of the Limoges town hall.

summary: A wave of nationwide unrest in France, which initially began as high school demonstrations over poor conditions, escalated into large-scale protests against high living costs, systemic inequality, and police force. In Limoges, masked demonstrators set fire to a police car outside the 143-year-old town hall before breaking in and starting a blaze that gutted the structure and caused its bell tower to collapse. Regional Prefect Maurice Barate confirmed that two-thirds of the historic building was lost, describing it as a deliberate act. Similar demonstrations, featuring looting and vandalism, took place in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux, and Lille. Security forces responded with tear gas and water cannons. According to officials, hundreds of thousands participated nationwide, leading to numerous detentions and injuries among law enforcement officers.
response: According to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, at least 60 law enforcement officers were injured and over 1,200 people were detained in the nationwide police response. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the destruction.

crowd.text: an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people take to the streets

injuries.text: at least 60 law enforcement officers were injured

updates.text: A wave of unrest swept across France as protests turned into violent clashes.
Protesters set fire to the historic town hall in Limoges, causing the bell tower to collapse.
